title: Retrieval: filters, hybrid search & reranking
summary: The first search is rarely the best one. This module covers everything between the question and the chunks a model reads: **search settings** (k, thresholds, MMR), **filters** (written by hand or by the model from the question), **time** (which version of a policy is in force), **hybrid search** (keywords and embeddings fused), **learned sparse vectors and ColBERT**, **reranking** with a cross-encoder, **query transformations** (multi-query, HyDE, step-back, decomposition), **parent-document** retrieval and **contextual compression**. Production's retriever becomes hybrid + reranked + time-aware: hit@1 0.64 → 0.82.
learn: **Retrievers**: one interface over k, score thresholds, MMR and filters
**Metadata filters and self-query**: hard constraints enforced exactly, with the model writing the filter
**Time-aware retrieval**: validity dates, 'as of' questions, recency boosts, dates in the prompt
**Hybrid search**: BM25 and embeddings fused by rank (RRF), and why tokenization matters
**SPLADE and ColBERT**: learned sparse vectors and late interaction in Qdrant
**Reranking**: cross-encoders, two-stage retrieval, FlashRank, Cohere, an LLM
**Query transformations, parent documents and compression**: better questions, bigger context, less noise
flow:
question ─(translate if non-ASCII)─→ query
   ├─ Postgres full-text (ts_rank) ─┐
   └─ pgvector HNSW (cosine)  ──────┴─ RRF fusion → 10 candidates (filter: valid today)
                                          └─ FlashRank cross-encoder → best k

labs.explain:
Production's chunks behind LangChain's **Retriever** interface: `invoke`, `batch`, piping into chains, metadata filters, and search types. The lab measures precision and recall across k on all 45 questions, a score threshold on an on-topic and an off-topic question, and MMR's variety.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

"Which vegan things cost less than 210 rupees?" has hard constraints that semantic search treats as words to resemble. The lab compares plain search, a hand-written **metadata filter**, and **self-query**: the model writes a search plan (query + filter fields) from the question, constrained by a schema.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

code.why: The schema is the guard rail: only these fields can be filtered.

labs.explain:
The corpus holds two handbooks: the archived 2024 edition (20 days of leave) and the current one (24 days). Both answer 'how many days of leave?'. The lab filters by **validity dates**, extracts the date from **'as of' questions**, boosts **recent notices** with a half-life, and shows what **dates in the prompt** change.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

code.why: Production: validity dates from the document registry onto every chunk.

labs.explain:
Six questions where one method or the other fails (an email address, a GSTIN, a paraphrase), through **BM25**, **dense**, **Reciprocal Rank Fusion** and LangChain's **EnsembleRetriever**; then all 45 questions, including BM25 with its default tokenizer.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

Beyond one vector per chunk: **SPLADE** (a sparse vector of word weights that also adds related words), dense vs sparse vs hybrid collections in **Qdrant**, and **ColBERT** (a vector per token, scored by MaxSim) as a reranker, with what each stores per chunk.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

**Bi-encoders** (embeddings) encode the question and each chunk separately; **cross-encoders** read them together. The lab fetches candidates with embeddings and reorders them with **FlashRank** (a local cross-encoder), on four questions and all 45; plus an **LLM** reranker and Cohere's hosted one (when a key is set).

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

notes.text: Question and each passage scored together.

labs.explain:
Improve the question before searching: **multi-query** for vague questions, **HyDE** (search with a hypothetical answer), **step-back** (the general rule behind a specific case) and **decomposition** (one search per sub-question), plus LangChain's MultiQueryRetriever.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

Small chunks match precisely; big sections hold whole answers. Index something small (child chunks, a **summary**, or **questions** the section answers) and return the **parent** section. Measured on the handbook and contract questions.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

Retrieved chunks are mostly context around one useful sentence. An **embedding filter** keeps similar sentences for free; **LLM extraction** copies out only what answers (checked for verbatim copying). The lab measures the characters saved.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

path.title: Production path: Nimbus retriever v3
path.summary: The production Retriever now searches the way the evaluation said is best: **hybrid** (Postgres full-text + pgvector, fused by RRF) for 10 candidates, **reranked** by a local cross-encoder (FlashRank), among documents **valid today** (validity dates from a document registry). On all 45 questions against the real index: hit@1 0.64 → 0.82, MRR 0.727 → 0.874, for about 65 ms more per question.

steps.title: Validity dates
steps.explain: A document registry (`data/nimbus/.documents.json`, standing in for a content system) gives documents `valid_from` / `valid_to`. Ingestion stamps them on every chunk (two new metadata columns, added by a small migration), and the retriever filters to documents valid on the question's date: today unless the caller passes another. The archived 2024 handbook no longer answers today's questions.

notes.text: Existing tables get the new columns; re-ingestion fills them.

production: Have the system that owns a document (HR, legal) own its dates too: a registry nobody updates is worse than none.
Log which version answered: auditors ask.

steps.title: Hybrid search
steps.explain: `search_mode=hybrid` runs Postgres full-text search (to_tsvector / ts_rank, with a GIN index) and the HNSW vector search, each for `search_candidates` results, and fuses them with Reciprocal Rank Fusion. Exact strings (emails, order ids, GSTINs) come from full-text, paraphrases from vectors.

notes.text: An expression index: no extra column to keep in sync.

production: Postgres's English text search stems words and drops stop words; product codes with punctuation may need the 'simple' configuration.
RRF ignores score sizes: a weak keyword match can outrank a strong vector match. The reranker after it corrects that.

steps.title: Rerank
steps.explain: `rerank=flashrank` scores each candidate together with the question (ms-marco-MiniLM-L-12-v2, ~22 MB, local) and keeps the best k. 10 candidates beat 20 and 40 here: more candidates added latency without finding more answers.

notes.text: Candidates among documents valid on the day that this audience may read.

production: The reranker runs on the CPU per request: watch p95 latency under load and cap candidates.
Re-measure when the corpus or language mix changes: ms-marco models are English.

steps.title: Evaluate
steps.explain:
The production Retriever against the Postgres index, all 45 questions:

| configuration | hit@1 | hit@3 | hit@5 | MRR | p50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v2 · dense | 0.64 | 0.80 | 0.89 | 0.727 | 39 ms |
| hybrid (RRF) | 0.69 | 0.87 | 0.93 | 0.779 | 42 ms |
| dense + FlashRank 10 | 0.80 | 0.91 | 0.91 | 0.852 | 105 ms |
| **hybrid + FlashRank 10** | **0.82** | **0.93** | **0.93** | **0.874** | 103 ms |
| hybrid + FlashRank 40 | 0.80 | 0.93 | 0.96 | 0.869 | 412 ms |

All rows filter to documents valid today, which already lifted plain dense search (the archived handbook no longer competes).
production: The query transformations (multi-query, HyDE…) and parent retrieval aren't on by default: each costs model calls per question and the evaluation didn't show a failure they fix. Keep them for question types where it does.
Track hit@1 if the model reads only the top chunk; hit@k if it reads k.
